newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EUROPEANS SHARE CONCERN ABOUT EMPLOYMENT -MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: EUROPEANS SHARE CONCERN ABOUT EMPLOYMENT -MINISTER.

text.p: Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn said on Sunday there was a common concern in Europe about lack of employment but no naive belief this could be solved through extra spending.
"There is a common concern that employment growth is unsatisfactory," he told reporters as he arrived for a meeting of EU finance ministers.
"How you address that is a matter of debate. There is no naive belief in extra spending," he said.

He reaffirmed there were no demands whatsoever for a change in the text of the EU's so-called stability pact, a framework for keeping EU budgets from ballooning in deficit after the planned launch of the new single European currency in January 1999.
Ministers were, however, discussing the text of a resolution on employment.

The finance ministers' meeting over dinner preceeded a two-day summit of EU leaders due to start on Monday that was originally supposed to culminate in agreement of a new treaty mapping Europe's course for the next century.

But the summit looks set to be dominated by a rift that has emerged between France and Germany since the new French government said last week that it wanted more time to study the stability pact. New French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said he wanted more attention paid to the bloc's double-digit unemployment.
